title: gen_sprites.py now emits sprites.json order (small_biz/campus before pucks) that mismatches sprites.odin's pinned positional binding — regenerated sidecar silently mis-binds bboxes for indices 6-10
evidence: tools/gen_sprites.py main() emits: `build_flat("host", HOST_FILL, HOST_SIZE, 1.20); names.append("host")` / `build_flat("dc", DC_FILL, DC_SIZE, 1.60); names.append("dc")` / `build_flat("small_biz", SMALL_BIZ_FILL, SMALL_BIZ_SIZE, 1.20); names.append("small_biz")` / `build_flat("campus", CAMPUS_FILL, CAMPUS_SIZE, 1.95); names.append("campus")` / `for ports in (4, 8, 16):` ... `names.append("puck_%d" % ...)` and writes `json.dump({"res": RES, "order": names, "content_bbox": boxes}, f, indent=1)` — i.e. order = [house_0..3, host, dc, small_biz, campus, puck_1, puck_2, puck_3]. The untouched renderer pins the opposite order: `files := [SPRITE_COUNT]string{ "house_0", "house_1", "house_2", "house_3", "host", "dc", "puck_1", "puck_2", "puck_3", "small_biz", "campus", }` with comment `// sprite order (the sprites.json `order` array): // 0-3 house_{0..3} (coral/gold/sage/sky), 4 host, 5 dc, 6-8 puck_{1,2,3}, // 9 small_biz, 10 campus (story 5.11 additions)` and binds positionally: `for i in 0..<SPRITE_COUNT { name, okn := order[i].(json.String) ... arr, oka := boxes[string(name)].(json.Array) ... sh.bboxes[i][k] = f32(n)` — textures[i] comes from files[i], bboxes[i] from order[i]. The committed sidecar still holds the matching old order (`order: ['house_0', 'house_1', 'house_2', 'house_3', 'host', 'dc', 'puck_1', 'puck_2', 'puck_3', 'small_biz', 'campus']`). sprites_parse_boxes' guards (`len(order) != SPRITE_COUNT`, bbox value-range checks) pass on the new order — nothing detects the mismatch. sprite_puck_target also reads `base := sh.bboxes[6][2]` as the basic puck's width.
detail: First pipeline run (the PR's whole purpose) writes order[] ≠ files[]: puck_1's texture gets small_biz's bbox, etc.; sprite_puck_target's tier base becomes small_biz's width. Silent corruption the documented T2 re-bless would bless. Falsifies the PR body's "zero renderer code churn" and spec §4 "fixed names/order".
recommended_fix: In main(), append small_biz and campus AFTER the puck loop to restore the renderer's pinned order (house_0..3, host, dc, puck_1..3, small_biz, campus); or make sprites_parse_boxes bind boxes by files[] name instead of position.

title: Spec and script header claim the CURRENT script re-renders byte-identical to the committed sprites — the determinism proof was run on the OLD script; the shipped script changes every PNG
evidence: docs/silhouette-spec.md:14-15: "The **pipeline is validated**: re-rendering the current script on Blender 5.2.0 LTS is pixel-deterministic (decoded pixels byte-identical to the committed sprites; only PNG-encoder metadata differs)." and :120: "The current script re-render is pixel-deterministic, so a no-op re-render is golden-safe". tools/gen_sprites.py:14-17: "Pipeline VALIDATED on Blender 5.2.0 LTS: the render is pixel-deterministic (decoded pixels byte-identical to the committed sheet; only PNG-encoder metadata differs), so a no-op re-render is golden-safe". The PR body states the validation artifact was different code: "**Deterministic render proven**: re-running the OLD script on Blender 5.2.0 LTS reproduces the committed PNGs pixel-for-pixel" — and this same diff replaces that old geometry (chimneys, wings, LED spheres deleted), so the shipped script's output is NOT byte-identical to the committed sheet.
detail: After this PR, "the current script" renders new geometry; re-running it changes all 11 PNGs, requiring the T2 re-bless. The docs' "no-op re-render is golden-safe" invites an accidental all-sprite regen believed golden-safe — against "No sprite change without documented golden impact".
recommended_fix: Reword both docs: determinism was validated with the pre-rework script; the shipped script changes every sprite PNG, so any re-render + commit requires the cause-documented T2 re-bless.

title: Render contract states two different outline expansions: README "footprint + ~0.03" vs spec §0 "footprint + ~0.06" (code expands 0.03 per side = 0.06 total)
evidence: assets/blender/README.md:26: "| Outline | thin dark ink `#33414F` plate at the base, footprint + ~0.03 (≈2px in-game ring) |" under heading "## Render contract (must match or the pass is rejected at fold-in)". docs/silhouette-spec.md:29: "| Outline | thin dark ink plate `#33414F` at base, footprint + ~0.06 (≈2px in-game ring) | MM's defining edge |". tools/gen_sprites.py: `OUTLINE_RING = 0.03   # ink ring width around the fill` and add_outline: `add_cube(name + "_o", (cx, cy, OUTLINE_H / 2), (fw + 2 * OUTLINE_RING, fd + 2 * OUTLINE_RING, OUTLINE_H), ...)` — 0.03 per side, 0.06 total.
detail: The two docs the user sculpts against give conflicting values for the same must-match contract; a sculpted pass following the README produces a half-thickness ring vs spec/code.
recommended_fix: State one convention identically in both docs, e.g. "outline ring 0.03 per side (footprint +0.06 total)".

title: Contract pins "ORTHO ~66° tilt" but the pipeline's camera elevation is pad-dependent (~47°-65° across the new pads); campus renders at ~47°
evidence: docs/silhouette-spec.md:26: "| Camera | ORTHO, ~66° tilt (roof carries the read, thin outline visible all around) | the MM top-down view (7.1 canon) |"; assets/blender/README.md:23: "| Camera | ORTHO, ~66° tilt — the roof carries the read, thin outline visible all around |". tools/gen_sprites.py aim(): `co.location = (0, -4.5 * pad, 10.0)` / `direction = mathutils.Vector((0, 0.35, 0.10)) - mathutils.Vector(co.location)` — elevation = atan(9.9 / (4.5·pad + 0.35)): house pad 1.12 → ~61°, host/small_biz 1.20 → ~60°, dc 1.60 → ~53°, campus 1.95 → ~47°, puck 0.95 → ~65°. _pr_body.md:75: "**Camera-tilt quirk left as-is** (pre-existing: tilt varies slightly with the per-sprite pad)" — the new pads widen the spread from ~51-61° to ~47-65°.
detail: The must-match contract value matches no sprite exactly and campus is 19° off; a user sculpting at a literal 66° gets different depth foreshortening than the pipeline's own renders. "Varies slightly" understates an 18° range.
recommended_fix: Either make aim() compute a constant-elevation camera, or replace "~66°" with the actual per-sprite tilt/pad table in both contract docs.
